verdict_reason: The RED is WITHDRAWN: the corrected _max_explainable_variance_truncsvd now reproduces sklearn's actual TruncatedSVD.explained_variance_ratio_[0] exactly. Re-measured on BLME's own 1000-vector gpt2 pools at all 12 layers against both sklearn algorithms: max relative error 7.30e-15 (randomized default) and identical under arpack. My counterexample layer is closed -- BLME 0.01069011 vs sklearn 0.01069011 at the first block output, where it previously read 0.5796 against 0.0107. The other four reported layers now read 0.98204511 / 0.97472746 / 0.94632680 / 0.72134938, matching sklearn to <= 1.6e-15 at each. The direction v0 is taken from the UNCENTERED SVD and both variances are CENTERED, which is what sklearn does; ddof=1 cancels between numerator and denominator so it is equivalent to sklearn's np.var. The per-word path is confirmed untouched and still exact: _max_explainable_variance matches sklearn PCA(n_components=1).explained_variance_ratio_[0] to <= 1.8e-15 on the same pools, which is what analyze.py::variance_explained_by_pc uses. The composition is right too: the released artifacts give 0.1601 (variance_explained.csv, official layer 1) - 0.298 (embedding_space_stats.json) = -0.138, the paper's own adjusted value, confirming adjusted MEV = PCA-per-word minus TruncatedSVD-EVR-pool. All three original kernels (SelfSim, IntraSim, MEV) remain parity-exact to <= 4e-16.
comparable_reason: Unchanged by this fix except that the pool1k pair is now comparable to the paper's own published values. Prior 10-model measurement stands: no emitted feature is a size proxy (r(d_model) = -0.079 self_similarity_corrected, -0.005 intra_corrected, +0.012 mev_corrected_sizematched, +0.094 mev; |rho(n_layers)| <= 0.38). The standing caveat is over-correction: self_similarity_corrected tracks the anisotropy_baseline it subtracts at r = -0.967 and intra_corrected at -0.722, and both corrected columns are emitted alongside that baseline, so the trio is near-perfectly collinear. The two MEV corrections remain estimated at different n (raw at a median of 9 occurrences, the pool baseline at 1000); the code says so and emits both without privileging either, which is the right call, but they must not be mixed.
github_reason: Re-verified this round against the same sources. kawine/contextual analyze.py:105-111 uses PCA(n_components=1).explained_variance_ratio_[0] for the per-word MEV (the TruncatedSVD object fitted beside it is used only to write components_[0]); analyze.py:182-184 uses TruncatedSVD(n_components=100).explained_variance_ratio_[0] for the pool baseline. sklearn defines that ratio as np.var(X @ V.T, axis=0) / np.var(X, axis=0).sum() -- identical in 1.7.0 and in the 0.20.X/0.21.X sources contemporary with the paper. BLME's helper now equals it to 7.30e-15 on all 12 gpt2 pools under the randomized default and to the same precision under arpack; the per-word helper equals sklearn PCA to <= 1.8e-15. The end-to-end pipeline remains unrunnable (the h5 embedding dumps and the sampled SemEval-STS inputs were never released), so kernel-level parity plus the released CSV/JSON artifacts is the strongest available check.
paper_reason: Three of four quantities reproduce and the fourth is now the official estimator. (1) SelfSim: BLME 0.9058/0.8903/0.8158/0.7645/0.9489 vs released 0.9205/0.9080/0.8495/0.8397/0.9854 at official layers 1/3/6/9/12, rel -1.6% to -9.0%. (2) 'roughly 0.6' random-word cosine in layers 2-8: released mean 0.5894, BLME mean_anisotropy_baseline 0.6183. (3) The pool baseline improved at four of five layers with the fix: released 0.298/0.998/0.997/0.994/0.829 vs BLME now 0.0107/0.9820/0.9747/0.9463/0.7213 (-1.6%, -2.2%, -4.8%, -13.0% at layers 3/6/9/12, against -3.1%, -3.5%, -7.1%, +17.3% before). Official layer 1 remains far off (0.0107 vs 0.298) but that is a corpus difference -- WikiText passages versus the paper's SemEval-STS sentences -- not an estimator difference, since the estimator now agrees with sklearn to 7e-15. (4) Raw per-word MEV is still +24% to +335% above the released values; I tested and refuted the context-distinctness explanation last round (<= 1.1% effect), leaving the BPE-token-id tracking unit and the corpus.
confounds_reason: Unchanged and not re-measured: the prior 10-model sweep found |r(d_model)| <= 0.253 (all p >= 0.48), |rho(n_layers)| <= 0.38, |rho(log vocab)| <= 0.66 for every emitted feature, and the one pure tokenizer statistic (n_words_tracked, pearson -0.850 with log(vocab) over 13 tokenizers) is behind the _meta_ prefix and excluded by feature_selection.py. This fix changes only the pool baseline estimator.
defects: ARCHIVE INCOMPATIBILITY, not recorded: mean_mev_baseline_pool1k moves 0.8810 -> 0.7270 and mean_mev_corrected_pool1k moves -0.3255 -> -0.1716 on gpt2, with a sign flip at the deepest reported layer (-0.1610 -> +0.0897). task_metadata.py carries such a note for geometry_prediction_alignment and geometry_matrix_entropy but none for this task; archived runs must not be pooled with new ones under these two keys.

The anisotropy correction over-corrects: self_similarity_corrected has r = -0.967 with the anisotropy_baseline it subtracts (raw SelfSim +0.864), intra_corrected -0.722, and all three columns are emitted together.

MEV's n-dependence is unchanged and is why the two baseline conventions disagree in sign: on an isotropic null at d = 768 the expected MEV is 0.2754 at n = 5, 0.1464 at the corpus median n = 9 and 0.0046 at n = 1000. Both protocols are emitted and neither is privileged, which is correct, but a consumer must not average them.

layers_reported is still a list of numpy.int64 (contextualization.py:471); plain json.dumps rejects it and BLME's writer masks it with default=str, so the emitted file reads ["0","2","5","8","11"] as strings rather than integers.

The aggregate means still include the last layer, where gpt2's anisotropy baseline is 0.9446 and raw MEV 0.8111, while the paper's headline figures deliberately quote layers 2-11 and treat the last layer as an outlier.

The anisotropy pool is silently min(num_samples, len(dataset)) vectors; the task's own built-in fallback dataset has 50 sentences, which would yield a 50-vector 'uniformly randomly sampled 1K' baseline with no warning. Production is safe because core.py sizes the shared corpus to the largest task num_samples.
fix: Nothing further is needed for correctness -- the estimator now matches the official to 7e-15 and the per-word path was never touched. Housekeeping only: (1) add the ARCHIVE INCOMPATIBILITY note to task_metadata.py for mean_mev_baseline_pool1k / mean_mev_corrected_pool1k (0.8810 -> 0.7270 and -0.3255 -> -0.1716, with a sign flip at the deepest reported layer); (2) cast layers_reported with int(); (3) emit a layer-2..L-1 aggregate alongside the all-layer mean; (4) warn or record a _meta_ field when the anisotropy pool is under 1000 vectors; (5) state in the docstring that the tracking unit is BPE token ids rather than spaCy word types, which is what puts raw MEV above the released values; (6) consider reporting corrected values as ratios, since corrected and baseline are r = -0.97 collinear.
